question: What is the ruling on udhiyah (qurbani), and is it wajib or sunnah?
answer:
Udhiyah, of course, is the sacrifice that is done to please Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala during the days of sacrifice. And it begins from the Fajr of the 10th of Dhul Hijjah, or technically from praying the Eid salah, because udhiyah is done after the Eid salah. So from the Eid salah of the 10th of Dhul Hijjah all the way up until before Maghrib of the 13th of Dhul Hijjah, according to one opinion, and according to the other opinion up until Maghrib of the 12th of Dhul Hijjah. There's a bit of a controversy: what are the days that you can sacrifice in? One opinion is up until the 13th day, and the one that probably most of you are aware of is up until the 12th day, right before Maghrib.

And sacrificing is one of the greatest actions of worship during these days, and Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala mentions in the Qur'an:

> فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ

And Ibn Abbas said this ayah is about udhiyah on the days of Hajj. And our Prophet ﷺ sacrificed every year. And one year the Sahabah said, "Ya Rasulallah, what is this sacrifice for?" He said, "Sunnatu abikum Ibrahim," this is the sunnah of our father Ibrahim. So they said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the blessing of the sacrifice?" He said, "For every hair on the animal, you shall get a good deed."

And Abdullah ibn Umar said the Prophet ﷺ spent 10 years in Madinah, and every year he made an udhiyah. Every year, without exception, he made an udhiyah.

By the way, it is called udhiyah from duha, Salat al-Duha, because typically the udhiyah is done in the early morning, and that's why udhiyah means in the early morning. Salat al-Duha, and duha is early morning. So udhiyah typically is done early morning, but it is not a condition, by unanimous consensus. You can do udhiyah at midnight. You're not going to be very smart by doing that, but still, no problem. You want to do it at midnight, go for it. It can be done. But typically, when is udhiyah done? Early morning. That's why it is called udhiyah.

And you may use any large domesticated animal. These are called bahimah in the Arabic language: cows, camels, sheep, goats, lambs. And each one has particular characteristics. There is no need for this open Q&A to go into advanced animals. If somebody is in Peru, let them ask, can we do a llama or not? Otherwise, for our purposes, if you have a llama, then let's take a look at it rather than eat its meat. No problem, inshallah. But these are the standard animals that our scholars have mentioned.

Now, the big controversy over udhiyah. Everybody agrees it's good to do. The big controversy, in a nutshell: is it wajib or is it sunnah? And the Hanafi madhhab, as all of us from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh know, says that udhiyah is wajib. And that is why in our countries, mashallah, tabarakallah, the streets flow with blood during this season. Most of our brothers from that land are not aware that in Arab lands it's not as much blood flowing, because in the Shafi'i madhhab and the Hanbali madhhab and the mu'tamad of the Maliki madhhab, the udhiyah is not obligatory. So the three madhhabs say udhiyah is a strong sunnah, and the Hanafis say udhiyah is what? Wajib.

But for whom? For the one who can financially afford it. By unanimous consensus, the one who is poor does not have to do udhiyah. If you cannot afford it, it's forgiven. But the Hanafis say that the one who can afford it must do it.

And I'm not going to go into the evidences on both sides, because it's a very big detail, and inshallah, whatever you follow is fine. But I just want to mention one hadith in Tirmidhi; actually, it's a statement from Ibn Umar. A man came to Ibn Umar and he said, "O Ibn Umar, is udhiyah wajib or not?" Ibn Umar said, "The Prophet ﷺ performed the udhiyah, and so did the Muslims." The man said, "Don't you understand my question? I'm asking you, is it wajib? I'm not asking what he did." So Ibn Umar said, "And don't you understand my answer? The Prophet ﷺ did, and the Muslims did."

Al-Tirmidhi commented on this and he said: and this hadith is the action of the ahl al-'ilm, that the udhiyah is not wajib, but it is a sunnah from the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, and people should do it. So Ibn Umar didn't want to get technical. The man is saying, "Is it wajib? Is it wajib? Is it wajib?" Ibn Umar said, "Look, the Prophet ﷺ did it, the Prophet ﷺ did it, the Prophet ﷺ did it."

And from this, Imam al-Tirmidhi and the majority of 'ulama, as I said the three madhhabs, and more than them. In fact, from most of the Sahabah it is authentically narrated, in al-Bayhaqi's Sunan and others, it is authentically narrated that Abu Bakr and Umar and Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas and a number of Sahabah occasionally did not do the udhiyah, to demonstrate to the people that it is not obligatory. But it is sunnah, and it is strong sunnah, and it is strongly encouraged.

And for the Hanafi madhhab, to be a little bit more advanced: most of the madhhabs divide things into five categories, and that is fard or wajib, and then sunnah, and then mubah, and then makruh, and then haram. But the Hanafis have seven categories, and they make a distinction between fard and wajib, and they put the udhiyah in the wajib, not the fard. So even they don't put udhiyah in the highest category; they make it one level below. And the other madhhabs, they say udhiyah is a strong sunnah. So the Hanafis and the other madhhabs are very close to each other, because of the technical issues. **The bottom line: if you can afford it, do it, bismillah.** No problem, okay?

As well, in the hadith in Sahih Muslim, our Prophet ﷺ encouraged people to eat some, to give some, and to give charity with some. So from this "some, some, some," the majority of scholars said it is mustahabb to divide it into three categories. It's not wajib; it is mustahabb to divide it into three categories. Give to the fuqara' a good amount, give to your family and friends a good amount, and, mashallah, have a feast, and invite me as well, and have a good amount as well. No problem, inshallah.

As well, the hadith of Jabir radiyallahu 'anhu, reported in Sahih Muslim: "We performed Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, and we sacrificed a camel on behalf of seven people and a cow on behalf of seven people." Hadith in Sahih Muslim. Therefore, from this we derive that the udhiyah of a camel suffices seven and not one.

As well, the hadith of Aisha: the Prophet ﷺ performed the udhiyah, she said, for himself and for his family. Which means for every family there is one udhiyah. You do not have to have five sheep. If you have, mashallah, three children, and you and your wife, you don't have to have five sheep. One sheep or one goat or one lamb for one family, or one seventh. Of which animal? Cow or camel. But we're in Texas, so we have to add buffalo. In Texas, buffalo; maybe longhorn, the steer. That's also one seventh. So if all seven families come together... It doesn't matter if you have zero kids, one kid, ten kids: each family should try to do one udhiyah, whether it's wajib or mustahabb. I already explained the difference between the madhahib.

The final point of udhiyah is that our Prophet ﷺ said: once the ten, the 'ashr of Dhul Hijjah, begin, whoever wants to perform the udhiyah, let him not trim the nails or the hair. Now, this is not to the level of tahrim; that's for the hujjaj. It is to the level of makruh. Makruh: try to not do it. If you do, there is no sin, and there is no kaffarah. You don't have to go and feed 10 people or free a slave or something; nothing like that. If you do, you are not like the hujjaj. The hujjaj have a penalty if they shave or trim or whatnot. But the mudahhi, the one who's giving the udhiyah, there is no penalty. But it is not sunnah; it is makruh. You should avoid it.

As well, the one who is encouraged to do this, not required, is the one who's paying for the udhiyah, not the family members of the mudahhi. So the one who's paying for the udhiyah. Why? Because our Prophet ﷺ did not tell his women and the children in the household anything, what to do. He said: whoever is going to do the udhiyah, let that person... So the one who's paying for the udhiyah: that's the ruling for the 10 days. Try your best.

Why? So that you get to the spirit of the hujjaj. That's all that it is: you feel like you are participating in the Hajj. This is not for the hajji himself. The hajji himself, if he's doing tamattu', between the umrah and the tawaf, they will trim and whatnot; no problem. The hajji himself has a different ruling. But for the one not doing Hajj, that is that.
